info.description: Local test collection for the ZifIQ Kotlin/Spring Boot backend -- covers only the modules with real persistence and business logic (Auth, Tenants & Members, OTP, VAT Control, Settings, Factory Setup, Factory Production, Factory Trading, Inventory Stock, Inventory Operations, NRS Reference Data, Customers). The remaining scaffolded modules (Account, AI, Barcode, Cashier, History, Invoicing, Menu, Process Guide, Showroom) still return hardcoded mock data server-side and are intentionally excluded until they're built out for real. Run folders top-to-bottom in order (01 through 12) -- each request's Tests script captures IDs/tokens into collection variables that later requests reuse, so the whole collection can be run end-to-end with Postman's Collection Runner with no manual edits. See docs/00-02 in the backend repo for the full design spec these endpoints implement.

request.description: Self-service root-tenant bootstrap. Run this first -- every other request depends on the token/tenant/credentials it creates. The email uses Postman's {{$guid}} dynamic variable so re-running this request never collides with a previous run's account -- no need to reset the database between test passes. Every later request that needs these credentials (Login, Forgot Password) reads them back from the registeredEmail/registeredPassword variables this sets, instead of a hardcoded literal, so they never drift out of sync.

item.description:
Customers & Distributors (backend docs/04). Needs 01 - Auth > Register Tenant first (for the token); everything else this folder needs it creates itself, so it can be run on its own right after Register Tenant.

Run top to bottom - requests are lettered by area and each one sets up the next:
A setup (a home location) - B dealer categories - C correspondents - D registering customers of every type - E search, filters and pickers - F wallet/deposit ledger, adjustments, reversals - G promotion/demotion - H status - I rules that span records - J dealer self-service.

Requests marked "(error: ...)" deliberately break a business rule and assert the exact error code, so a full run is all green. Captured variables: customerLocationId, today, goldCategoryId, diamondCategoryId, correspondentId, correspondent2Id, dealerId, dealerName, dealerCode, customerId, specialId, walkinId, adjustmentEntryId, reclassificationId.
